[[EuroLeague]] | team = Real Madrid | position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] | number = 33 | college = * [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] (2017–2020) * [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2020–2021) | high_school = [[INSEP]] ([[Paris]], France) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team1 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[Oklahoma City Blue]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team3 = [[Raptors 905]] | years4 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team4 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years5 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team5 = →[[Cleveland Charge]] | years6 = 2026–present | team6 = [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA G League champions|NBA G League champion]] ([[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]]) * Third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2020) }} '''Olivier Sarr''' ({{IPAc-en|oʊ|ˈ|l|ɪ|v|j|eɪ|_|ˈ|s|ɑːr}} {{respell|oh|LIV|yay|_|SAR}},{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}} {{IPA|fr|ɔlivje saʁ}}; born 20 February 1999) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He is the older brother of basketball player [[Alex Sarr]]. ==Early life and career== Sarr started playing basketball at age three with his father, a former player, and drew inspiration from [[Hakeem Olajuwon]].{{cite web |title=Eurohopes interviews Olivier Sarr |url=http://www.eurohopes.com/news/6300/eurohopes_interviews_olivier_sarr |publisher=Eurohopes |accessdate=22 July 2020 |date=29 March 2020}} He played for club teams Bouscat and TOAC before joining [[INSEP]], a sports institute in [[Paris]].{{cite web |title=Olivier Sarr |url=https://godeacs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/olivier-sarr/5115 |publisher=Wake Forest University Athletics |accessdate=22 July 2020}} He competed for [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball|Centre Fédéral]] in the [[Nationale Masculine 1]] and represented INSEP at the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation Tournament]].{{cite web |last1=Le Pape |first1=Etienne |title=Direction Kentucky pour Olivier Sarr |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-ncaa/direction-kentucky-pour-olivier-sarr.html |publisher=BeBasket |accessdate=22 July 2020 |language=French |date=6 May 2020 |archive-date=22 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200722182810/https://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-ncaa/direction-kentucky-pour-olivier-sarr.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |last1=Geisinger |first1=Brian |title=Better Know a Player: Is Wake Forest's Olivier Sarr the ACC's next stretch-5? |url=https://accsports.com/acc-analytics/better-know-player-wake-forest-olivier-sarr-accs-next-stretch-5/ |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |accessdate=22 July 2020 |date=14 June 2018}} Sarr moved to the United States when he was 15 years old.{{cite web |last1=Lima |first1=Rafael |title=Spotlight: Olivier Sarr |url=http://wfuogb.com/2019/09/spotlight-olivier-sarr/ |website=[[Old Gold & Black]] |accessdate=22 July 2020}} He was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Scout.com|Scout]] and committed to [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] over offers from [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] and [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]].{{cite web |last1=Engel |first1=Charlie |title=Has Wake Forest landed a new French Superstar? |url=http://wfuogb.com/2017/04/has-wake-forest-landed-a-new-french-superstar/ |website=[[Old Gold & Black]] |accessdate=22 July 2020}} ==College career== Sarr averaged 3.2 points and 3.0 rebounds per game as a freshman at Wake Forest. He gained 20 pounds going into his sophomore season.{{cite news |last1=Harmon |first1=Dowell |title=Olivier Sarr becoming a threat for Wake Forest Basketball |url=https://247sports.com/college/wake-forest/Article/Olivier-Sarr-becoming-a-threat-for-Wake-Forest-Basketball--139951619/ |accessdate=1 August 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=6 December 2019}} As a sophomore, Sarr started 16 games and averaged 6.2 points and 5.5 rebounds per game, leading the team with 25 blocks.{{cite news |title=Ex-Wake Forest Center Olivier Sarr Transferring To Kentucky |url=https://www.wuky.org/post/ex-wake-forest-center-olivier-sarr-transferring-kentucky#stream/0 |accessdate=1 August 2020 |work=WUKY |date=6 May 2020}} On 29 February 2020, Sarr scored a career-high 37 points and grabbed 17 rebounds in a 84–73 victory over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{cite news |title=Sarr, Wake Forest deal blow to Irish NCAA hopes |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168574 |accessdate=1 August 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=29 February 2020}} As a junior, Sarr averaged 13.7 points and 9.0 rebounds per game and had 11 double-doubles. He was named to the Third Team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]]. After coach [[Danny Manning]] was fired, Sarr entered the transfer portal. In May 2020, he announced he was transferring to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] after receiving interest from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] and [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]. Sarr applied for a waiver for immediate eligibility at Kentucky.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Givony |first2=Jonathan |title=Olivier Sarr to transfer to Kentucky from Wake Forest |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29142654/olivier-sarr-transfer-kentucky-wake-forest |accessdate=1 August 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=6 May 2020}} He, along with fellow transfer Jacob Toppin, received immediate eligibility on 21 October 2020.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Olivier Sarr, Jacob Toppin eligible for Kentucky Wildcats after NCAA transfer waivers |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30164249/olivier-sarr-jacob-toppin-eligible-kentucky-wildcats-ncaa-transfer-waivers |accessdate=21 October 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=21 October 2020}} Sarr averaged 10.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game. He declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing the additional season of eligibility granted by the NCAA due to the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news |last1=Kennedy |first1=Bryan |title=Olivier Sarr foregoing remaining eligibility, to declare for NBA Draft |url=https://www.wtvq.com/2021/04/20/olivier-sarr-forgoing-remaining-eligibility-to-declare-for-nba-draft/ |access-date=23 June 2021 |work=WTVQ |date=20 April 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2021–2024)=== After going undrafted in [[2021 NBA draft]], Sarr played for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the [[2021 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Olivier-Sarr/Summary/72293|title=Olivier Sarr|work=RealGM.com|access-date=28 December 2021}} On 16 October 2021, he was signed and then immediately waived by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|first=JD|last=Shaw|title=Thunder Sign Olivier Sarr, Justin Jaworski|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/thunder-sign-olivier-sarr-justin-jaworski.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=16 October 2021|access-date=16 October 2021}}{{cite web|title=Thunder Waives Diakite, Jaworski and Sarr|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder-waives-211016|website=NBA.com|date=16 October 2021|access-date=16 October 2021}} He subsequently joined the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League]], posting 14 points and 7 rebounds in his debut versus the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{cite news|title=G-League: Jaylen Hoard and Olivier Sarr start well with the Blue|url=https://news.in-24.com/sports/basketball/189157.html|work=News in 24|date=7 November 2021|access-date=9 November 2021|archive-date=9 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211109123229/https://news.in-24.com/sports/basketball/189157.html|url-status=dead}} On 27 December, Sarr signed a 10-day contract with the Thunder{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Three Players to 10-Day Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder-signs-three-211227|work=NBA.com|date=27 December 2021|access-date=28 December 2021}} and re-joined the Blue on 6 January 2022.{{cite web|title=2021-2022 G League Transactions|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/transactions/league/2022|work=RealGM.com|access-date=8 January 2022}} Three days later, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Thunder.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Olivier Sarr to Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/sarr-220109|website=NBA.com|date=9 January 2022|access-date=9 January 2022}} He was reacquired and activated by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] on 19 January. On 21 February 2022, Sarr signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Thunder.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Olivier Sarr to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-sarr-220221|website=NBA.com|date=21 February 2022|access-date=21 February 2022}} He was waived by the Thunder on 6 April 2022.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Melvin Frazier Jr. to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/frazier-220406|website=NBA.com|date=6 April 2022|access-date=6 April 2022}} Sarr joined the [[Phoenix Suns]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Phoenix Suns 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612756/suns |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On 7 September 2022, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] announced that they had signed Sarr.{{Cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Devontae Cacok, Isaiah Miller, Jared Rhoden And Olivier Sarr To Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-devontae-cacok-isaiah-miller-jared-rhoden-and-olivier-sarr-to-contracts|date=September 7, 2022|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 7, 2022}} On 13 October, the Trail Blazers announced that they had converted their contract with Sarr to a [[two-way contract]].{{Cite web|title=Trail Blazers convert Olivier Sarr to a two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-convert-olivier-sarr-to-a-two-way-contract|date=October 13, 2022|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 13, 2022}} On 18 November, the Trail Blazers announced that they had waived Sarr. He never played a game for the team.{{Cite web|title=Portland Trail Blazers Sign Ibou Badji to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/portland-trail-blazers-sign-ibou-badji-to-two-way-contract|date=November 18, 2022|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 18, 2022}} On 11 January 2023, Sarr was re-acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|date=11 January 2023|access-date=11 January 2023}} On 13 February, he signed a two-way contract with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Olivier Sarr to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-sarr-230212|website=NBA.com|date=13 February 2023|access-date=13 February 2023}} and on 21 August, he signed another two-way contract with the Thunder.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Olivier Sarr to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-sarr-230821|website=NBA.com|date=21 August 2023|access-date=22 August 2023}} In the [[2023–24 NBA season]], Sarr made 15 appearances for the Thunder, averaging 2.3 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 0.1 assists in 6.5 minutes per game. On 15 April 2024, Sarr suffered a [[Achilles tendon rupture|ruptured Achilles]] in the OKC Blue's G-League Finals victory over the [[Maine Celtics]].{{Cite web|title=OKC Thunder's Olivier Sarr suffers ruptured Achilles tendon|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2024/04/17/okc-thunders-olivier-sarr-suffers-ruptured-achilles-tendon/|access-date=April 22, 2024|website=okcthunderwire.usatoday.com|language=en}} ===Raptors 905 (2025–2026)=== On 1 August 2025, Sarr signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web |title=RAPTORS SIGN SARR {{!}} Toronto Raptors |url=https://raptors.com/news/raptors-sign-sarr |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=raptors.com |language=en}} He was released by the Raptors on 16 October.{{Cite web|title=Raptors Waive Five Players|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-five-players|access-date=October 23, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} He subsequently joined the [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]], the Raptors' G League affiliate. ===Cleveland Cavaliers / Charge (2026)=== On 3 March 2026, Sarr signed a two-way contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Olivier Sarr to Two-Way Contract|url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/cavaliers-sign-olivier-sarr-to-two-way-contract|access-date=March 8, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} ===Real Madrid (2026–present)=== On 15 August 2026, Sarr signed a two-year deal with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Olivier Sarr supplies size, versatility to Real Madrid|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/olivier-sarr-supplies-size-versatility-to-real-madrid/|date=August 15, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=August 16, 2026}} ==National team career== Sarr played for [[France men's national under-17 basketball team|France]] at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] in [[Zaragoza]], Spain. He averaged 4.4 points and four rebounds per game and helped his team finish in sixth place. At the [[2017 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in Slovakia, Sarr averaged 7.6 points and 5.4 rebounds per game for the sixth-place team. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
